entry.title: Remove the exit ritual: a Practice session climbs the rung
entry.content:
Remove the exit ritual: a Practice session climbs the rung

The exit ritual was the only unlock path: `/ritual` dealt two sentences from
the module's comprehension pool, `/verdict` made the single write, and the
production counters (`exit_available`, every sentence of the rung marked) were
the gate in front of both. All three are gone. Finishing a Practice session
climbs the rung, on its last card — `Session.tsx` calls `completeRung` in an
effect the moment the summary appears, and the summary names the rung and hands
the Ladder the unlock beat instead of offering a way on.

The first rung's session is now ten cards. `planSession` used to pad a short
ladder up to fifteen by repeating the rung from its first sentence; on the very
first rung, where nothing has been passed, that was five cards that taught
nothing — and, now that the last card is the climb, five cards standing between
the learner and a rung already worked through. Every later session is fifteen,
as before.

What went with the ritual: both routes and their screens, `engine/comprehension.ts`,
the `exitAvailable` predicate and the `exit_available` / `exit_ready` states it
fed, the `handover`/`cameFrom` tokens, `hint.production`, and ten strings.json
keys across nine courses. `passRitual`/`completeRitual` are `passRung`/
`completeRung`; `engine/exit.ts` is `engine/production.ts` and reads counters
rather than deciding anything.

What stayed: the counters, as a record of the rung rather than a door — the
module list's dots and `n / 10` still read them; the comprehension pool in the
authored content and the shipped module files, because it is authored work
across nine courses and retiring it is a content change, not a screen one; and
the two lines the verdict ended on, moved to the summary that says them now
(`practice.climbedRung`, `practice.climbToLadder`), so no course is asked for a
new translation.

TYPES ok | LINT ok | TEST 809/810 | CONTENT ok | FONTS ok | BUILD ok | BUDGET ok
— the one red is `scripts/generate-splash.test.ts`, which fails identically on
a clean checkout of the base commit (the PNGs do not regenerate byte-for-byte
on this machine).

Walked live at 360px against `npm run dev` (hi-mr): first rung, hub promises 10,
session serves 1/10..10/10, summary reads "M1 · पार" over "सीढ़ी पर चढ़ो",
storage shows L1-M1 passed with its ten sentences enrolled and the snapshot
cleared, and the Ladder plays the beat once on M2. Second rung: hub promises 15,
session serves 15, L1-M2 passes, queue at 20, ladder at "Level 1 · 10 में से 2".

entry.title: Docs: en-ko's L4 wave-3 review, and the first two L5 brief decisions …
entry.content:
Docs: en-ko's L4 wave-3 review, and the first two L5 brief decisions (#562, #550, #565)

en-ko's section closes the L4 review chain: docs/94-102 now each carry all three waves against a
complete forty-module ladder.

The two L5 decision docs are the first written against a ladder with four verified levels under it,
and en-ar's found three holes that are the level's real work:

- **No verb of understanding anywhere.** `afham`, `fahimtu` both free, and no key among the 1,095
  contains `fahm` or `fham`.
- **No verb of knowing.** `aʿrif`, `aʿlam`, `adrī`, `ʿaraftu` all free.
- **No word for "or".** `aw` and `am` both free; the only `aw`-initial keys in the whole course are
  `awlād`, `awwal` and `awwalan`. L2-M9 taught choosing between two things without ever buying the
  disjunction.

All three land on L5-M8 "When words run out", which is the module for exactly that.

Also from en-ar, two spellings the parts column forbids: never `a-lā`, because the hyphen buys a
one-letter key `a`; and never `bi-aḍ-ḍabṭ`, because `aḍ` is the one sun-letter prefix docs/87 §3
did not list as owned.

And one deferral that lands nowhere, named as a hole rather than passed on: the dual as a system
went L3 → L4 → L5 and stops here. Its `-ān`/`-ayn` split IS case, which L2-M1 rule 4 forbids
writing, and the course already ships both sides inconsistently — `kitābān` at L1-M8 against
`yawmayn` and `marratayn` at L3-M7. That is a law amendment and an issue against L1-M8, not an
authoring wave.

Four courses asked for a lower `newWordCap` on their M10, as en-it and en-de did at L4. The cap is
a pinned invariant at 25 and the test asserts it, so the number stays and each argument moves into
its own module's notes, where an author reads it — sharper at L5 than at L4, because this is the
last rung of the last level and a key it leaves unpaid is unpaid forever.

entry.title: Content: L4 Nuance closes on all nine courses — 360 modules, four com…
entry.content:
Content: L4 Nuance closes on all nine courses — 360 modules, four complete levels (#537, #552-#562)

Forty-five modules in the closing wave, ninety across the level, and every course now stands at
L1-M1..L4-M10. `content/<course>/levels.json` has L4 `draft: false` on all nine.

The wave's finding, and it is the level's: **ownership is per FORM, not per lexeme, and an L4
module's siblings are in the index too.** Every course hit it:

- en-de: `warten` is L3-M4's while `warte` and `wartet` are free; `arbeiten` L1-M4's, `arbeitet`
  free; `bleiben` L2-M10's, `bleibt` free. Eight displays were rerouted rather than mint rows.
- en-fr: `fermé` and `annulé` were listed free by an L4-M7 brief and are L4-M2's — a sibling of the
  same level, two waves earlier. `en fait` is L4-M4's, and L4-M10's brief uses it in its own worked
  example.
- en-es: `retraso` is L4-M2's, `aquel`/`aquella` L4-M3's, `tengas` L4-M5's — all four listed free.
- hi-en: `earlier` is L4-M3's, `closed` L4-M1's, both listed fresh.

A brief's INDEX SEAM is a photograph. en-es watched its own fold move three times inside one wave:
837 surfaces through L4-M5, 885 through L4-M7, 949 through L4-M10.

Three defects the checks caught that no brief could have:

- hi-en's `noticed` row listed `notice` in its forms, and `content:shown` answered
  `RE-TEACH … L4-M7 owns the key` — the noun was opened three modules earlier in the same wave.
- hi-en's `going` is untaught after thirty-nine modules: `go`/`goes` are L1-M4's, `going to` is
  L1-M6's WHOLE, `gone` is L4-M3's, and the bare participle was never spent. A quoted line was
  rewritten rather than given a row.
- en-de: a span's key is order-sensitive. `Damals gab es …` folds to `gab es`, not `es gab`, so the
  brief's own pattern would have shipped an unreachable row.

Two authoring slips fixed here rather than bounced back, both course laws a wave cannot see because
the guard sits behind a count assertion that goes stale mid-wave: hi-en L4-M9-S07 shipped a
mnemonic with no Devanagari (#270), and en-ko L4-M6-S03 had a word row with no note at all.

entry.title: Tools: check-shown sees the keys a hyphen buys, not just the surface …
entry.content:
Tools: check-shown sees the keys a hyphen buys, not just the surface written

en-ar's L4-M4 wave worked out that a whole frame silently buys its hyphen PARTS — `ʿalā ar-raghm
min` buys `raghm`, `min al-mumkin an` buys `mumkin` — and therefore that L4-M5 must not open a bare
`mumkin` row. It reached that by reasoning about `surfaceIndexKeys`, because the check could not
see it: the intra-module map was keyed on whole surfaces alone, so a row opening a word an earlier
row had already bought as a part was invisible. Working it out from the emitter is the wrong way
round; the check should say it.

Only the WHOLE key is tested, though every earned key is now recorded. Part against part is not a
defect and flagging it is noise — the first cut of this change did flag it and printed twenty
findings on shipped content, almost all of them en-ar's `al-`: every definite noun donates the part
`al`, so two ordinary nouns in one module read as a collision. Nobody taps a bound article. What is
forbidden is a row whose own display is a word another row already earned.

L3 and L4 are clean under the wider check on all nine courses.

L1 and L2 are NOT, and that is a real backlog rather than a false positive: hi-mr L2-M1 has one row
listing `द्या` in its forms while another row displays it, L2-M2 has three rows sharing one
possessive paradigm, and there are more. It is the same class this session already fixed in hi-mr
L3 (ddbb3c8) and en-es L3-M1, now visible one level lower. Not swept here — three authoring waves
are in flight against those files' descendants — and recorded so the sweep is a deliberate change
rather than a surprise.

Docs: the en-ar L4 wave-2 review (#539)

Its modules went in with d765886; the review section follows.

Nine seam corrections, and two are the same class wave 1 found on `yusabbibu`: `aẓunnu` and
`aʿtaqidu` are free while `aẓunn` and `aʿtaqid` are L3-M3's, so writing the fully vowelled form
would have minted a second key for a verb the ladder already owns. This course does not write mood
endings, and the index is where that shows up.

The finding worth keeping is about the emitter rather than the language: a whole frame silently
buys its hyphen PARTS. `ʿalā ar-raghm min` buys `raghm`, `min al-wāḍiḥ anna` buys `wāḍiḥ`,
`min al-mumkin an` buys `mumkin` — so L4-M5 opens no bare `mumkin` row. The agent reached that by
reasoning about `surfaceIndexKeys` rather than by running the check, because the check could not
see it; `tools/check-shown.ts` is being taught the case now.

Also recorded: the mood citation in the wave instructions is still wrong. It says "L2-M1 rule 4",
which is the adverbial `-an` rule; the no-mood law is L3-M4 rule 4, handed forward by L3-M2 rule 3.

entry.title: Content: L4-M3..M5 complete on all nine courses (#528, #538-#546)
entry.content:
Content: L4-M3..M5 complete on all nine courses (#528, #538-#546)

The rest of the wave — en-ar's three, en-es's and en-ru's, and the L4-M1..M2 files that were still
in flight when e770be8 went in. Every course now stands at L4-M1..M5; CONTENT ships 315 modules
strict, 35 on each.

Two findings about METHOD, both worth more than the modules they came from.

**Never grep for a surface; ask the fold.** en-ru's L4-M5 brief opens on "the verb TO KNOW is not
taught anywhere in this course", justified by a scan of the index for any `zna`-initial surface.
The shipped surface is `zná`. The grep was blind to the acute, and `znáyesh'` is L2-M6's — inside
`Ty znáyesh', gde magazín?`, which is exactly the sentence the module was going to teach around.
The three keys the module opens are genuinely free, so it ships, but as a point-back rather than a
first teach. A grep over romanized text misses the accent, over Devanagari a matra, over Arabic the
hamza convention. That instruction is now in every remaining wave prompt.

**The checker catches what the brief cannot.** en-es shipped `esperes` with `espere` in its forms
and `content:shown` answered `RE-TEACH L4-M4-S05 "espere": L3-M8 owns the key` — L3-M8 spent it as
the usted command *please wait*. Same spelling, different job, and the row's own note would have
been unreachable. This is the paradigm-hole rule from e770be8 arriving from the other direction:
there, a cell a lower level owns; here, a homograph that means something else.

Three more the briefs did not say:

- en-ru: `skazáli` is free while `skazál` is L2-M10's, so the brief's "points back at L2-M10" was
  not available — different key, own row, per the never-edit-below law. And `s odnóy storoný` earns
  exactly one key, so the three bare words the brief lists as fresh stay free for a later module.
- en-es: `yo` is still free after thirty-two modules. Not a seam — a hole. No display writes a bare
  `yo`; `yo diría` is spent whole, and the gap is flagged for a later wave.
- en-es: `ido`, `hecho` and `perdido` are L3-M7's, so docs/86 §4's own worked regrets
  (`debería haber ido`) could not be written as briefed; the module uses `llamado` and `salido`.

entry.content:
Content: L4-M3..M5 as the wave lands, eight courses in (#528, #538-#546)

Twenty-three of the wave's twenty-seven modules, committed at a point where `content:validate` is
`CONTENT 311/311 ok` — which is the gate that says every file on disk is complete rather than
half-written. en-ar's three are still being authored and follow.

The wave's most generalisable finding, from en-it and confirmed independently by en-fr: **a
paradigm row must have a HOLE wherever a lower level owns that cell.** `avrei` can carry its whole
conditional paradigm; `sarei` cannot, because `sarebbe` is L3-M4's, so the third person is
deliberately absent from the forms list. `volevo`/`volevi` have the same shape — `voleva` is
L3-M5's. en-fr's `serais` row omits `serait` for exactly the same reason. A complete-looking
paradigm that swallows an owned cell is either a collision or an unreachable row, and no brief
warned of it; the rule is now written into every remaining wave prompt.

Three more the briefs did not say:

- en-de: `gute` is free while `guter` is L3-M2's, so `eine gute Idee` printed a shown-but-untaught
  on first draft; `möglich` is untaught anywhere in the course; and `wissen` is free while `weiß` is
  L2-M3's, so an infinitive in a hedge would have shown an untaught surface. Two of the three were
  rewritten rather than given rows.
- en-fr: `n'aurais` and `n'aurait` are their own keys — the elided negative conditional is not
  covered by `aurais` — so without them in `forms` two displays are each a shown-but-untaught.
- en-it: two keys would have raised `maxSpan` from 3 to 4 (`vale la pena di`, `non è detto che`) and
  were stated in prose instead of bought.

entry.title: Docs: the en-ko L4 wave-1 review (#536)
entry.content:
Docs: the en-ko L4 wave-1 review (#536)

Its modules landed in 26ebcb4; the review doc follows because it was still being written.

Three seams the brief had wrong, and the first is the sort that only shows up when someone tries to
write the sentence. The M1 brief's joined-auxiliary ruling rests on `bwayo` and `bwasseoyo` being
owned, which they are — but nobody checked `boseyo` and `bogo`, the instruction and sequential
shapes of the same verb, and `content:owner` says both are free after thirty modules. S02's own
pattern cannot be written without them.

The other two are arithmetic the brief got wrong in the same direction:

- `V-ge dwaesseoyo` was said to "spend nothing on `ge`". Endings are never hyphenated on this
  course, so the shown token is the whole word — `salge`, `hage`, `gage` are one fresh key each.
- An owned noun is not an owned particle form: `ireum` is L1-M1's but `ireum-eul` is free,
  `hoesa` is L3-M2's but `hoesa-e` is free. Two planned sentences were dropped rather than mint a
  particle form of a lower level's noun.

And one course law caught a pattern the brief invited: `BARE_PARTICLES` forbids writing `i` as its
own token, so the demonstrative "this N" the M1 pattern list asks for is unwritable — every one
became `igeo-reul` or dropped the demonstrative.

The wave's one re-teach is deliberate: L4-M2-S04's `ttaemune` is L3-M3's, every other word in the
sentence is owned, and the clause extension the sentence teaches is carried by the module rule and
the trap rather than by a note no learner can reach.

entry.title: Content: L4-M1 and L4-M2 on all nine courses (#519, #529-#536)
entry.content:
Content: L4-M1 and L4-M2 on all nine courses (#519, #529-#536)

Eighteen modules, nine agents at once, no worktrees: each owned only
`content/<course>/modules/L4-M1..M2.json` and its own review doc, and nobody ran a command that
writes `public/content/`. The parent builds once before and once after — which is what made a
shared checkout safe where the L3 waves needed isolation.

Two harness bugs the wave exposed, both of the same shape — a level's number written into a check:

- `tools/check-shown.ts` read `L2-M10.json` as "the shipped index" and folded `L3-M*.json` off disk
  by name. An L4 author would have got a fold with no L4 in it, so every surface their own L4-M1
  opened would have come back untaught in L4-M2. It now takes the deepest emitted index by
  `cumulativeThrough` length and reads the level off the module id.
- `tools/delta-index.test.ts` compared the delta set against `cumulative.get('L3-M10')`, so it went
  red the day L4-M1 landed — a fact about the ladder growing, not about the fold. It reads the last
  module off the built index now.

And one the wave found in the test harness itself, reported independently by hi-en, en-ar and
en-de: `src/course/types.test.ts`'s per-course guards (`expect(hiEn.length).toBe(30)`) run BEFORE
the loop they guard, and vitest aborts the case there — so while a census number is stale, every
language law in that block silently does not run at all. hi-en's and en-ar's agents each
re-executed those assertions by hand to check their own work. The counts are updated and the hi-en
guard now says in its message what it is protecting.

What the index overturned this wave:

- en-de: the ladder holds the `ich`-form of most earlier verbs and almost never the third person —
  `macht`, `trinkt`, `denkt`, `isst`, `fährt`, `bleibt` are all free while their first-person forms
  are owned. Any L4 sentence conjugating an older verb in the third person shows an untaught
  surface. `warten` is the outlier and M2-S06 was written `Wir warten …` to route around it.
- en-es: `primero` is L2-M4's, inside an ordinal row noted on `la primera calle`, so a why-tap on
  `Primero calienta el agua` returns a note about street numbering.
- en-fr: `parce que` is L1-M9's but `parce qu'il` is not, and the elision leaves the FIRST token
  unowned — so a fronted `Parce qu'il …` is one shown-but-untaught `parce`. Every display here
  takes a consonant-initial subject instead.
- hi-en: `of` is L1-M8's, `make` is L3-M2's and `sure` L2-M6's — the briefs justified indexing
  `because of` and `make sure` whole from one owned half each; both halves are owned.
- hi-mr: "free" hides a class — a free key on an OWNED lexeme (`घाला` free, `घालतो` L3-M9's). It
  collides with nothing but still owes a note pointing back, and all six such rows carry one.

en-it needed no seam correction at all — all twenty of its fresh keys came back free and every
pointer in both briefs reproduced verbatim.

entry.content:
Tools: check-shown reads the deepest emitted index, not L2-M10, and folds any level

Two hard-coded assumptions from the level it was written for. It read
`public/content/<course>/index/L2-M10.json` as "the shipped index", which was true while L3 was the
level being authored and is now a level out of date; and it folded `L3-M*.json` off disk by name,
so an L4 author got a fold with no L4 in it and every surface their own earlier modules had opened
came back untaught.

The index file is now the deepest one — the file whose `cumulativeThrough` is longest, chosen that
way rather than by filename because `readdirSync` sorts `L1-M10.json` before `L1-M2.json`, the same
trap `tools/index-owner.ts` fell into on its first draft. The level to fold off disk is read off the
module id, so one check serves L3, L4 and L5.

entry.title: Content: the L4 Nuance briefs for all nine courses (#510, #520-#527)
entry.content:
Content: the L4 Nuance briefs for all nine courses (#510, #520-#527)

Ninety briefs — ten `Nuance` rungs on each of the nine courses — written by nine agents at once and
merged here, because `tools/course-briefs.ts` is one file and nine authors cannot share it. Each
wrote a fragment and its own decisions doc (docs/85-93) and nothing else, so there was no conflict
to resolve: the fragments are spliced in verbatim.

Every INDEX SEAM claim in them was checked with `npm run content:owner` against the real fold of
all thirty shipped modules, and the recurring finding is worth stating once: **a module's own
headline word is usually already spent.**

- en-ar lost two whole module plans. The cause module's vocabulary is all L1-M9's, so M2 is built
  on `fa-`, the consequence clitic; and L3-M4 shipped `laytanī dhahabtu maʿaka ams` outright — the
  counterfactual AND the wish — so M3 became `kāna` as an auxiliary.
- en-es would have taught sentence-initial causal `como`, which is L1-M4's, where it means "I eat".
- en-fr's `-er` imperative is a homograph of the `je` form, so `mange`, `travaille`, `parle`,
  `demande` and `reste` are all owned; the index picked the module's verb list.
- hi-en's "Back then" cannot own the habitual past — `used to` is L3-M10's — so it owns habitual
  `would`, itself L2-M5's, as a third job on that row.
- en-de's modal particles are all owned except three (`mal`, `eben`, `halt`), and `da` is L2-M7's
  presence adverb, so M2 may never teach causal `da`.
- hi-mr has never taught `but`. After thirty modules `पण` came back free, which moved it to M2 and
  left M4 the concessive proper.
- en-ru has never taught "to know": `znáyu`, `znat'`, `znáyete` all free, and M5's own pattern
  rested on it.
- en-ko found that a `forms` array MINTS KEYS: `docs/76` §4 says `-deon` "never earns a bare key",
  and L3-M9-S04 lists bare `-deon` in a row's forms, which `normalizeSurface` strips to a key.

Two overrides applied on merge, both recorded in the briefs' own notes rather than discarded:
en-it and en-de each asked for a lower `newWordCap` on M10 to make "nothing new is needed" a bound
rather than a hope. The cap is a pinned invariant at 25 (PRD §5) and the test asserts it, so the
number stays and the argument moved into the notes, where an author reads it.

One test change the briefs forced: `src/course/types.test.ts`'s en-ko -mnida gate is scoped to
L1-L3 rather than "not L1". L4-M7's whole job is the announcement register as a productive system,
so above L3 a -mnida form is the content, not a style slip. The gate is narrowed, never deleted —
an L2 sentence reaching for `hamnida` still fails.

entry.title: Docs: the en-fr L4 brief decisions (#525)
entry.content:
Docs: the en-fr L4 brief decisions (#525)

Planned against 783 surfaces folded over 30 modules through L3-M10, maxSpan 4.

The seam that decides M1: the `-er` imperative is a homograph of the `je` form, so `mange`,
`travaille`, `parle`, `demande` and `reste` are ALL already owned — L1-M4's, L2-M7's, L3-M5's,
L3-M4's. The index therefore chooses the module's verb list, not the pedagogy: `regarde`,
`écoute`, `tourne`, `prends`, `attends`, `mets` all came back free.

Two places docs/74 is wrong, recorded rather than inherited: it says `c'était` stays L2-M10's, and
an index-file scan finds that key only in `L3-M10.json`; and its "whole surface" phrasing for
`il faut` and `je voudrais` is loose — only the bare `faut` and `voudrais` are owned, the phrases
are free.

The hyphen seam is live on this course in three new places: `pourriez-vous` buys bare `pourriez`,
`États-Unis` buys both parts, and `billet aller-retour` buys `retour` while `aller` is L2-M4's.

Two mechanics checked against the real tokenizer rather than assumed. A character census over all
thirty en-fr modules finds no quotation mark anywhere, so M10's guillemets are a genuine addition —
and `tokenizeSurface("Il m'a dit : « Tu es en retard »")` drops the guillemets and the colon
entirely, so the quoted line costs the index nothing.

Bounds 12 -> 13 -> 14, and the 13 is load-bearing: six of the ten modules are structurally two
clauses, and twelve words forces a stub second clause. Open questions 58-81 continue docs/82.

entry.title: Docs: the en-ar L4 brief decisions (#521)
entry.content:
Docs: the en-ar L4 brief decisions (#521)

Planned against 840 surfaces folded over 30 modules through L3-M10, maxSpan 5.

Two modules had to be rebuilt around what the index actually holds. The cause module's obvious
vocabulary is all L1-M9's — `bi-sabab`, `li-ʾanna`, `li-ʾannī`, `li-ʾannahu`, `li-dhālika` — so M2
is built on `fa-`, the consequence clitic, and the three-way split `wa` / `thumma` / `fa-` that
English collapses into "and". And L3-M4 already owns the counterfactual and the wish: `la-`,
`la-kuntu`, `laytanī`, `idhā` are all spent, and L3-M4 shipped `laytanī dhahabtu maʿaka ams`
outright — so M3 is `kāna` as an auxiliary instead: `kāna qad`, `kuntu sa-`, past obligation.

`fī raʾyī` is L1-M9's, not L3-M3's as docs/70 §3 records. The doc names the index as the authority
so the error is not inherited a third time.

The level-wide correction: L4's grammar is largely MOOD, and this course does not write mood
endings (L2-M1 rule 4), so every brief specifies `li-yadkhul`, `qabla an adhhab`, `kuntu adrus` —
never the fully vowelled forms. `adrusu` is free and `adrus` is L3-M2's, which is what the law
requires.

Bounds 12 -> 14, repeating L3's shape one notch higher: new morphology at 12, because a sentence
should not pay for a new shape and for length at once. Open questions 62-86 continue docs/78.

entry.title: Docs: the en-es and en-it L4 brief decisions (#520, #524)
entry.content:
Docs: the en-es and en-it L4 brief decisions (#520, #524)

Two more of the nine, each planned against what `npm run content:owner` reports rather than
memory: en-es 715 surfaces through L3-M10 (maxSpan 3), en-it 958 (maxSpan 3).

**en-es.** The index forced the level's biggest content decision: sentence-initial causal `como`
was M2's obvious first teach, and `como` is L1-M4's — it is "I eat". A module teaching `Como no
tenía tiempo…` would resolve its own headline word to a row about eating, the same shape as the
`का` bug. M2 teaches `ya que` and names `como` in usage only. Two more of the same class: `corta`
is L2-M2's, the feminine of `corto` in a sentence about short hair, so a cooking `corta el pan`
would resolve to a haircut; and `donde` is free while `dónde` is L1-M7's, because an accent is a
letter and the two are different keys.

**en-it.** Three of L4-M1's imperatives were already spent by L2-M4's directions module — `vada`,
`prenda`, `giri` — and L3-M3's brief had listed `vada` as fresh, which first-occurrence-wins made
wrong; L4 inherits the correction rather than repeating it. `alla fine` is L2-M10's, not L3-M10's
as L3-M10's own brief claimed. Two went the other way and are what let this level buy its central
contrasts cheaply: `già`, `ancora` and `però` are all still free after thirty modules.

Bounds climb 12 -> 14 on both, continuing L3's 10 -> 12, and are set by sentence SHAPE rather than
by position: instructions are short whatever level they sit at, a two-clause counterfactual will
not fit in twelve.

One correction applied on merge: en-it's M10 asked for `newWordCap: 20` to make "nothing new is
needed" a bound rather than a hope. The cap is a pinned invariant at 25 (PRD §5) and
tools/course-briefs.test.ts asserts it, so the number stays 25 and the argument moved into the
module's notes, where an author reads it.
